subject.title: [Feature] Decouple dreaming from memory-core — allow any memory plugin to implement dreaming protocol

question: Should OpenClaw define a stable Plugin SDK/manifest dreaming provider protocol, or keep built-in dreaming as memory-core-owned behavior with external ClawHub sidecar/plugin implementations?
rationale: Current main has selected-plugin dreaming config and a memory-core sidecar engine, but query/promote/report/scheduler ownership would be a new public plugin API and config contract that automation should not invent without maintainer direction.

options.title: Design a provider protocol
options.body: Approve an SDK/manifest RFC for dreaming lifecycle capabilities, update docs/exports/contract tests, and make memory-core one provider implementation.

options.title: Keep memory-core ownership
options.body: Document that built-in dreaming remains memory-core-owned and point vector-native implementations to ClawHub packages such as memory-lancedb-dreaming.

options.title: Defer to multi-slot memory
options.body: Track the request under the broader memory role-slot architecture before adding a dreaming-specific API.

recommendation.title: Design a provider protocol
recommendation.body: Approve an SDK/manifest RFC for dreaming lifecycle capabilities, update docs/exports/contract tests, and make memory-core one provider implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: History shows broad recent ownership across dreaming helpers, docs, and related gateway/doctor surfaces, making this the best available routing candidate for the product/API decision.
